takeaway: The vagus is parasympathetic, rest and digest: it stimulates gastric chief cells to secrete pepsinogen and increases gut motility.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the vagus nerve is correct?

answer.text: Activation of the vagus nerve stimulates chief cells in the stomach.

lines.text: The vagus nerve, cranial nerve X, starts in the medulla and wanders down into the abdomen.
lines.say: The vagus nerve, cranial nerve ten, starts in the medulla and wanders down into the abdomen.

lines.text: Its stimulation is parasympathetic: rest and digest.
It stimulates the chief cells in the stomach to secrete pepsinogen.
It also increases intestinal motility, so the option saying it decreases motility is wrong.
The parietal cells get only an indirect push, through gastrin and histamine, to make acid.
So the correct statement: vagal activation stimulates the chief cells.
